draft_text: In Cheiro's reading, a head line that begins joined to the life line is associated with a sensitive, cautious disposition that may underrate its own abilities.
Benham reads a longer join between the head and life lines as less self-reliance and more reliance on others' advice.
caveat: Benham's age-dating of the join (W2-429b) is excluded.

draft_text: Heron-Allen treats a clear head line joined to the life line at its start and running toward the Mount of the Moon as the normal, favourable form: good sense, clear judgement and strength of will.
caveat: Needs the termination point observed; mounts are postponed, so this may be withheld in the MVP.

draft_text: Cheiro reads a small gap between the head and life lines as independence of thought and quick judgement.
open_issue: Define 'narrow' as a measurable gap before evaluation.

draft_text: Cheiro links a longer thumb with will-power guiding action; he reads a shorter thumb as more impulsive and stubborn.
open_issue: Define relative thumb length from image landmarks.

draft_text: In Cheiro's system the heart line concerns the affectionate and emotional nature, not physical health.
Cheiro associates the fate line with the broad course of one's career. The tradition does not let this reading foretell specific events.
Bṛhatsaṃhitā 68.43 treats deep, well-formed palm lines as an auspicious sign traditionally linked with prosperity, and shallow lines as the reverse.
caveat: Gloss is lighting-dependent and not evaluated; the finger-spacing clause is withheld.

draft_text: Bṛhatsaṃhitā 68.44 regards three lines rising from the wrist to the middle of the palm as a royal (highly auspicious) sign.
open_issue: Translation conflict: Iyer (1884) has three lines rising from the wrist to mid-palm; Zysk and Hastasanjivana vv. 39-41 read three wrist bracelets. The Sanskrit (tisro rekha manibandhanotthitah karatalopagah) needs a ruling from the Sanskrit reviewer. Until then, keep both readings and do not evaluate either.

draft_text: Bṛhatsaṃhitā 68.36 links long fingers with a comfortable life and smooth fingers without skin folds with popularity.
caveat: 'small = intelligent' and 'flat = serve others' are withheld pending review.

draft_text: Hastasanjivana reads clear bracelet lines at the wrist as auspicious: three traditionally mark royal standing, two a counsellor's standing, one prosperity.
caveat: The wrist must be in frame; the capture guidance currently asks only for the palm. The gendered left-hand rule is excluded.

draft_text: Hastasanjivana reads the upward line rising from the wrist by the finger it reaches; reaching the forefinger or middle finger is traditionally associated with authority and leadership.
